sections.label: Building the rules
paragraphs: With the new brand manual in hand, I established clear visual rules. Logo placement. Color specifications. Typography rules. Graphic elements and spacing systems. Every rule had to be flexible enough to work across print, digital, packaging, and merchandise.

sections.label: Consistent but flexible
paragraphs: The design system made the new brand consistent but not rigid. The core identity was strong enough that it would feel like Rokoko no matter where you encountered it.

sections.label: Presentation templates
paragraphs: I built templates for Google Slides so teams could create decks that felt branded without being designed. Took hours off presentation prep.

sections.label: Social media system
paragraphs: Social media branding covered Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube with templates and guidelines. Everything from grid posts to job listings to YouTube thumbnails carried the same visual language.

sections.label: Email templates
paragraphs: Email templates prioritized clarity and personality. Marketing could update them without rebuilding the layout. The tone was always friendly but professional.

sections.label: Packaging
paragraphs: Packaging for their first hardware product launch under the new brand was minimal but bold. The unboxing experience felt premium and deliberate, reflecting Rokoko's position in the market.

sections.label: Merchandise
paragraphs: Merchandise extended the brand into physical objects. Tote bags and t-shirts for events weren't afterthoughts, they were brand ambassadors.

sections.label: Consistency by default
paragraphs: After the rebrand, Rokoko had one cohesive visual language across every platform. The team could create new assets without consulting on every decision. Consistency became the default, not something that required oversight.

sections.label: Market perception
paragraphs: The unified brand system elevated Rokoko's perception in the market. They felt more polished, more trustworthy, more like a company making innovative products rather than experimenting with technology.

sections.label: The lasting lesson
paragraphs: What I learned from this work was the power of building systems, not just assets. The best contribution wasn't any single beautiful graphic, it was enabling the team to keep that consistency going even after I left.
